articles.title: FIR filed against contractor for submitting forged bank guarantee in MP
articles.description: Bhopal, Aug 5 (IANS) An FIR has been registered against a contractor for allegedly submitting a forged bank guarantee to secure four construction packages under the Madhya Pradesh Urban Development Company (MPUDC), officials said. The case was registered on Tuesday at the MP Nagar police station in Bhopal against the joint venture of South Gujarat Construction Company Private Limited and Engineering Professional Company Private Limited following a complaint by MPUDC. According to officials, the contractor had submitted a bank guarantee as part of the tender process for four construction packages. However, suspicion arose over the authenticity of the document during verification. A detailed inquiry by MPUDC allegedly found the bank guarantee to be forged, following which Urban Administration and Development Commissioner and MPUDC Managing Director Sanket Bhondve directed officials to initiate legal action. Based on the complaint, police registered a case under Sections 318(4), 336(3), 338 and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and launched an investigation. Section 318(4) pertains to cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property or valuable documents, while Section 336(3) deals with forgery of documents or electronic records with intent to commit fraud. Section 338 relates to forgery of valuable security, including bank guarantees, and Section 340(2) deals with using forged documents as genuine. "We found the bank guarantee submitted by the contractor to be forged during verification. Acting on the findings, instructions were issued to lodge an FIR and initiate legal proceedings," Bhondve said. He added that the department has adopted a zero-tolerance approach towards fraud in government works. "Any attempt to submit forged documents or indulge in financial irregularities in government projects will be dealt with strictly under the law," he added. The Police said the authenticity of the documents and the role of those involved are being investigated and further action would be taken based on the findings. The case comes amid increased scrutiny of documents submitted by contractors executing government projects, with authorities stepping up verification to prevent fraud and protect public funds. --IANS pd/khz

articles.title: India eyes record 20 GW distributed renewable capacity this fiscal
articles.description: India anticipates its highest distributed renewable energy capacity this fiscal year. Schemes like PM Surya Ghar and PM Kisan Urja are expected to exceed twenty gigawatts. articles.title: Gujarat govt imposes statewide ban on glue traps, citing animal cruelty
articles.description: Gandhinagar, Aug 4 (IANS) The Gujarat government has imposed an immediate statewide ban on the production, sale, storage and use of glue traps, commonly known as sticky boards, used to catch rats and other small animals, making the devices illegal across the state as part of a move to prevent cruelty to animals. The decision was announced through a resolution issued by the state's Agriculture, Farmers Welfare and Cooperation Department. The ban applies to the manufacture, sale, purchase, storage and use of glue traps with immediate effect. Glue traps are coated with a highly adhesive, non-drying substance that immobilises animals and birds on contact. According to the government, trapped animals often sustain serious injuries while attempting to escape and may eventually die from starvation, dehydration, suffocation or injuries caused during their struggle. The government said the use of glue traps violates Section 11(1) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960. It also noted that the Animal Welfare Board of India has classified the use of glue traps as highly cruel and illegal under its guidelines. In a parallel measure, the Industries and Mines Department has directed that glue traps be removed with immediate effect from the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) procurement portal as well as from other e-commerce and online platforms. The order also prohibits all government departments, boards, corporations and local self-government bodies from purchasing or using the devices. The resolution warns that any violation of the ban may attract legal action under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, and Section 223 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023, along with any other applicable provisions of law. District Police authorities and the Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SPCA) have been authorised to register complaints and initiate action against those found violating the prohibition. The government has directed traders to immediately stop stocking and selling glue traps, as their production, sale, purchase and storage are now prohibited. It has also advised members of the public not to use glue traps for rodent control in homes, offices or factories. Instead, citizens have been encouraged to adopt legally approved and animal-friendly alternatives, including cage traps and other non-lethal rodent control methods, in place of adhesive traps. --IANS mys/dan
